function: Multivariate fronthaul quantization for cell-free massive MIMO downlink: a neural codebook and gradient search choose each RU's transmit signal to minimize interference at UEs (p. 14-15).
system: Cell-free massive MIMO downlink, no RIS: 8 two-antenna RUs, 3 two-antenna UEs (p. 19); 4 RUs with 16 antennas, 4 four-antenna UEs (p. 20); band not stated.
method: Neural-MQ: per-RU fully connected neural codebook (one hidden layer) trained with Adam to minimize expected sum effective interference, unsupervised; bits found by annealed gradient descent (p. 15-18).
data_channel: 3GPP TR 38.901 UMi channel, fixed RUs, random UEs; training on 100 channel realizations and 100 Gaussian symbols; testing on five realizations, 1000 symbols (p. 18-19).
test_conditions: Default: training and testing at 18 dB, same UMi setting; trained with 1 or 4 UEs, tested with 1-8; trained at 10 dB, tested across SNR (p. 18, 22).
baselines: Conventional VQ and SMQ of [7] (Lloyd-Max codebooks); CP with MMSE precoding; infinite-fronthaul linear and non-linear precoding; neural-VQ, a neural-MQ variant (p. 17-20, 23).
metrics: Sum spectral efficiency, average symbol error rate with 16-QAM, and sum spectral efficiency versus normalized computational complexity (p. 19-20).
complexity: Table I orders: neural-MQ 2I·O(Σ_m D_m(B_m+D_m(K_m−1)+2N_m^tx)) at the DU, linear in sum fronthaul rate; α-PMQ T·O(2^max B_m); operation counts in Fig. 5 (p. 10, 16, 19).
q1_support: p. 19: "The channel is generated by following 3GPP urban micro (UMi) models [32]"; p. 26: "TR 38.901". The same setting covers the training (p. 18) and test (p. 19) channel realizations.
q2_support: p. 22: "training assumes a number N of UEs equal to either 1 or 4, while testing for N = 1, ..., 8 UEs"
q3_support: p. 20: "we compare neural-MQ to (i) infinite-fronthaul benchmarks; (ii) CP; and (iii) neural-VQ"; p. 23: "Neural-VQ follows the same procedure as in neural-MQ". Non-learned baselines are present (CP, conventional VQ and SMQ), but the only learned comparator is a variant of the proposed method; no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 16: "would require computational complexity of the order O(2I · Σ_{m=1}^{M} Dm(Bm + Dm(Km − 1) + 2Nm^tx)" and "which grows linearly with fronthaul sum-rate"; also Table I, p. 10.
notes: PDF is arXiv:2409.06715v1 (p. 1); its title and authors match the TSP paper of the DOI, which the preprint does not print. Borderline on Step 1 function: the paper says "Our work complements studies on precoding designs ... by focusing solely on fronthaul compression" (p. 4) and fixes MMSE precoding (p. 19). I included it as area 3 because the learned codebook and gradient search choose the RU transmit signals to minimize the UEs' estimation error (EI (42), p. 16), which the paper says "can leverage the benefits of non-linear precoding" and beats linear precoding with infinite fronthaul (p. 21); if the reviewer reads it as fronthaul compression alone, the decision is exclude, function, p. 4. Learned method graded: neural-MQ; alpha-PMQ is a graph-based search with Lloyd-Max/CVX codebooks. q1: the training sentence (p. 18) does not name the channel model, but the experiment captions state 3GPP UMi generation (p. 19-20). q3: VQ and SMQ of [7] use codebooks from the data-driven Lloyd-Max (K-means) algorithm (p. 10), but the paper calls them conventional PC schemes (p. 17-18), so I counted them as non-learned; if K-means codebooks count as learned, q3 becomes 1 (Fig. 5, p. 19, compares them with neural-MQ on sum spectral efficiency). Pages 3, 10, 12, 16 and 19-23 were read as images; the text layer of p. 12 holds hidden leftover text ("Rayleigh channel, single antenna") not visible on the page, which I ignored.
